paragraphs: Rabbi Anani bar Sasson. (Anani—[1 Chronicles 3:24](https://www.sefaria.org/I_Chronicles.3.24).) [Moed Katan 24b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.24b.7) mentions him expounding at the Nasi’s doorway. Rabbi Ami heard and objected: “Is it his own teaching? It is Rabbi Elazar’s in Rabbi Oshaya’s name!”

And in [Shabbat 64b](https://www.sefaria.org/Shabbat.64b.13-14) he said in the name of Rabbi Yishmael [in accord with Rabbi Yose]: everything is like a kavul. And see [Yerushalmi Shabbat 6:1](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.6.1.11), at the end of the halakhah.

He is also mentioned in [Zevachim 88b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.88b.4-5): he said, 'Like the dispute here,' etc., and likewise there he expounded why the section on sacrifices was juxtaposed to the section on the priestly garments, etc.[^3]

notes.text: The checked Moed Katan text explicitly names Rabbi Elazar. The Shabbat parallel names Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose; Hyman’s bracketed [כר׳ יוסי] is preserved as his supplied wording.

The consulted Moed Katan 24b explicitly names Elazar in Oshaya’s name. Shabbat 64b first has Yishmael and then Yishmael son of Yose; Hyman’s bracketed “in accord with Rabbi Yose” is kept separately rather than silently rewritten.

The linked Yerushalmi names Aniyani bar Sosai reporting Rabbi Eliezer in the neighboring discussion. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2911&lang=en) gives Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yose for the Bavli saying. The consulted Zevachim writes Inyoni bar Sasson in the two homilies.
